intro: Enter Didyma, a sanctuary in Aydın province whose story begins in the 8th century BC. This was the oracle sanctuary of Apollo, and its temple is one of the largest in Anatolia. Prepare to feel very small.
history: A sacred way linked Didyma to Miletus, and this was a major oracle. After Alexander's visit, work began on a colossal temple — but it was never finished.
structure-1: You are now standing before the Temple of Apollo, one of the largest temples ever attempted. It was some 500 years in the building, and still never finished. And here is a surprise: it never had a roof. Behind the forest of columns lay an open court, holding the oracle spring and the laurel tree.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Medusa head, the adyton and the Sacred Way.
facts: Did you know? Construction drawings used by the ancient architects can still be seen on the temple walls. The Temple of Apollo was designed with 122 columns, built over some 500 years, and never finished. Its columns stand 19.7 metres tall, making it one of the largest temples in the Greek world. And it was an oracle, linked to Miletus by a 17-kilometre Sacred Way that pilgrims walked.
outro: This brings our tour of Didyma to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water. The temple was never finished — perhaps that is why it still feels alive. Enjoy your visit.
